record.category: fully managed wide-column NoSQL database (Cassandra/DynamoDB API)

free_tier.stated: Developer Free Trial: a 30-day trial on smaller instances (e.g. AWS t3.micro); Production Evaluation: a 48-hour free trial of production-grade instances. One free trial per account.
free_tier.notes: Two time-boxed trials, not a perpetual free tier: 30 days on small instances and 48 hours on production-grade instances. No perpetual free cluster is published on the first-party pricing or docs pages.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: no per-object size cap stated on the first-party pages read; trial clusters are limited to the smallest indexing node size (AWS t4g.medium / GCP e2-medium, 2 vCPUs and 4 GiB RAM each)
per_object_cap.notes: The only published size constraint is the trial node size, not a single-object cap.

retention.stated: the free offering is a time-limited trial: 30 days for the developer trial and 48 hours for the production evaluation, after which a regular paid cluster is required
retention.notes: The 30-day figure is the developer trial length; the production evaluation is 48 hours. Both expire rather than delete data on a storage cap.

egress.terms: standard cloud-provider rates apply for Internet egress and inter-region transfer; no fixed free egress allowance is published on the first-party pages read

record.interface_detail: CQL binary protocol version 3 (Apache Cassandra compatibility) and the Alternator DynamoDB-compatible API; direct TLS connections on standard CQL ports with an IP allowlist. No dedicated CQL token exists in the interface vocabulary, so 'unknown' names it.
record.tooling: shard-aware CQL drivers (C++, Java, Python, Go, Rust), any CQLv3-compatible Cassandra driver, a Terraform provider, and ScyllaDB Monitoring; rclone does not apply
record.chaining: a free-trial CQL cluster reached over the public endpoint from a tunnel or a small worker gives a programme-accessible store for the trial window; the self-hosted ScyllaDB server is a last-resort option and is not a hosted free tier

limits.value: one 30-day developer trial or one 48-hour production evaluation per account
trial clusters limited to the smallest indexing node size: AWS t4g.medium or GCP e2-medium, 2 vCPUs and 4 GiB RAM

record.binding_note: Both free paths are time-boxed trials that expire (30 days or 48 hours) and require a paid cluster afterwards, so the clock binds before any storage or request cap.

identity_cost.detail: sign-up asks for a company email address, first name, last name and company name, or Google/GitHub/LinkedIn; no card is taken at sign-up, and payment information is prompted only when creating a regular paid cluster

record.reliability_note: trial clusters get no production SLA or backup guarantee; public-IP direct connections are intended for evaluation, and production uses VPC peering or PrivateLink.
record.confidence_note: First-party pages read on 2026-11-19: the pricing page (trials and billing), the free-trial docs, the quick-start docs (payment prompt), and the account sign-up page (identity gate).

evidence.quote: Developer Free Trial: A 30-day trial running on smaller instances (e.g., AWS t3.micro), perfect for exploring the CQL interface and building prototypes.
evidence.proved: a 30-day developer free trial runs on smaller instances

evidence.quote: Production Evaluation: A 48-hour free trial of production-grade instances.
evidence.proved: a separate 48-hour evaluation of production-grade instances

evidence.quote: The ScyllaDB Cloud free trial lets you explore ScyllaDB Cloud at no cost, including ScyllaDB drivers and monitoring. You get one free trial per account.
evidence.proved: one free trial per account, at no cost
the smallest trial node size on AWS
the account sign-up gate requires a company email address

evidence.quote: If not already provided, the wizard will prompt you to provide the required payment information.
evidence.proved: payment information is asked only on the regular paid-cluster path, not the free-trial path

record.notes: Hosted ScyllaDB Cloud offers two free trials on a vendor-managed cluster. A self-hosted ScyllaDB server is a last-resort option and is not a hosted free tier. The key distinction is trial-only: both free paths expire and there is no perpetual free cluster.
